topic.title: Alerts
topic.shortdesc: Provide contextual feedback messages for typical user actions with the handful of available and flexible alert messages.

section.title: Default alert
section.p: Alerts are available for any length of text, as well as an optional close button. Alerts are designed to be used with theme colors, but have neutral fallback colors for when no theme color is applied.

bodydiv.section: A simple alert — check it out!

section.codeblock: <section outputclass="alert"> A simple alert — check it out! </section>

section.title: Specialization
section.codeblock: <alert> A simple alert — check it out! </alert>

section.title: Variants
section.p: Use any of the eight variant theme classes for color mode adaptive, contextual styling (e.g., set outputclass to alert theme-success).

section.title: Additional content
section.p: Alerts can also contain additional HTML elements like headings, paragraphs, icons and links.

section.title: Well done!
section.p: Aww yeah, you successfully read this important alert message. This example text with a link is going to run a bit longer so that you can see how spacing within an alert works with this kind of content.
Whenever you need to, be sure to use margin utilities to keep things nice and tidy.

section.codeblock:
<i outputclass="bi bi-emoji-smile pe-2"/>Well done!

Aww yeah, you successfully read this important alert message. This example text with a link is going to run a bit longer so that you can see how spacing within an alert works with this kind of content.

Whenever you need to, be sure to use margin utilities to keep things nice and tidy.

section.title: Specialization
section.codeblock:
<icon outputclass="bi-emoji-smile" padding="e2"/>Well done!

Aww yeah, you successfully read this important alert message. This example text with a link is going to run a bit longer so that you can see how spacing within an alert works with this kind of content.

Whenever you need to, be sure to use margin utilities to keep things nice and tidy.

section.title: With icons
section.p: Similarly, you can use flexbox utilities and Bootstrap Icons to create alerts with icons. Depending on your icons and content, you may want to add more utilities or custom styles.

bodydiv.section: An example alert with an icon

section.codeblock: <section outputclass="alert theme-primary d-flex align-items-center"> <ph outputclass="bi bi-exclamation-triangle-fill flex-shrink-0 pe-2"/>An example alert with an icon </section>

section.title: Specialization
section.codeblock: An example alert with an icon

section.title: Notes
section.p: DITA note elements are displayed as alerts according to the type attribute. With the exception type="othertype", an icon is added if type is present.

example.note: This note will speed you on your way.
Don't forget to do what this note says.
This is a fine little tip.
Please pay extra attention to this note.
You can't do what this note says.
This is something other than a normal note.

body.codeblock: <note type="note"> This is just a note. </note> <note type="notice"> Notice this piece of information. </note> <note type="fastpath"> This note will speed you on your way. </note> <note type="remember"> Don't forget to do what this note says. </note> <note type="tip"> This is a fine little tip. </note> <note type="attention"> Please pay extra attention to this note. </note> <note type="caution"> Care is required when proceeding. </note> <note type="important"> This note is important. </note> <note type="restriction"> You can't do what this note says. </note> <note type="danger"> You may hurt yourself! </note> <note type="other" othertype="Another note"> This is something other than a normal note. </note>
body.p: The default colors can be overridden by using a theme attribute or an outputclass.

section.codeblock: <note type="note" outputclass="theme-primary"> This is a primary note.</note> <note type="note" outputclass="theme-secondary"> This is a secondary note.</note> <note type="note" outputclass="theme-accent"> This is accent note. </note> <note type="note" outputclass="theme-inverse"> This is inverse note. </note>

section.title: Specialization
section.codeblock: <note theme="primary-contrast"> This is a high contrast primary note. </note> <note theme="secondary-contrast"> This is a high contrast secondary note. </note> <note theme="accent-contrast"> This is a high contrast accent note. </note> <note theme="inverse-contrast"> This is a high contrast inverse note. </note>

body.p: Use an additional icon attribute or otherprops to alter the default icon.

example.note: This note has a search icon.
This note uses a styled smile emoji.

section.codeblock: <note otherprops="icon(bi-search)" type="other" othertype="Search"> This note has a search icon. </note> <note otherprops="icon(bi-emoji-smile), style(font-size: 2rem; color: cornflowerblue;)" type="note" othertype="Another note"> This note uses a styled smile emoji. </note>

section.title: Specialization
section.codeblock: <note icon="bi-search" type="other" othertype="Search"> This note has a search icon. </note> <note icon="bi bi-emoji-smile" style="font-size: 2rem; color: cornflowerblue;" type="note"> This note uses a styled smile emoji. </note>
